title: Text content
description: The `text` content block, the baseline result type that every tool result may carry.
question: Does text content reach the agent unchanged?
usage_note: Not published. Candidate source: count of public MCP servers using this capability. Not estimated, so the panel stays empty until the corpus is scanned.
why: This is the content type a framework is expected to handle, so it is the control row: the other content types can only be read as losses against a text block that survives.

notes.crewai: CrewAI: the text arrives stringified inside a Python list repr, as "['SENTINEL_TEXT_BLOCK']" rather than the block's text.
notes.genkit_js: Genkit (JS) 1.42.0: `processResult` returns `{ error }` for `isError`, `structuredContent` when the server sent one, the joined text (JSON-parsed when it looks like JSON) when every block is text, the lone block when there is one, and otherwise the whole `CallToolResult`. A text block reaches the model as text at every boundary, but beside `structuredContent` (`mixed_content`) only the structured value is returned and the text block is gone.
notes.mastra: Mastra 2.2.0: a result without `structuredContent` comes back unchanged, text block intact. When the result carries `structuredContent`, that value is returned in place of the whole result, so every content block, text included, is gone.
notes.pydantic-ai: Pydantic AI 2.54.0: text beside media blocks arrives as a plain string, byte-identical. When every content part is text and the result carries `structuredContent`, the typed value is returned in place of the text, so the text block is gone.
notes.google_adk: Google ADK 2.11.0: the tool's return value keeps each text block in `content`. The model receives the whole dumped `CallToolResult` as `FunctionResponse.response`, so the text arrives wrapped in JSON rather than as plain text.
notes.autogen: AutoGen 0.7.5: Text survives at every boundary on its own, but a result that also carries an audio or resource-link block makes `McpWorkbench.call_tool` raise, so the text in that result reaches the agent only as the error message.
notes.semantic_kernel: Semantic Kernel 1.45.0: boundary-dependent. `Kernel.invoke` returns a TextContent per block. The model's tool message is `str()` of that list, the Python repr of SK's content objects, so the text is inside a repr string.
notes.google_adk_js: Google ADK (TypeScript) 2.2.1: boundary-dependent. `MCPTool.runAsync` returns the `CallToolResult` unchanged (`afterToolCallback` sees it with every block intact), and ADK puts that object in the `functionResponse` of the next `LlmRequest`. At `direct` the text block is a text block. At `agent` the model reads it inside one JSON object, `{"content": [{"type": "text", "text": ...}], ...}`, never as a plain text part.
notes.spring_ai: Spring AI 2.0.1: the tool result reaches the agent and a direct `ToolCallback.call` as one string: the JSON of the result's content list with each block's `type` field dropped, e.g. `[{"text":"SENTINEL_TEXT_BLOCK"}]`. The text survives inside that JSON, not as a text block.
notes.beeai: BeeAI Framework 0.1.85: a text block survives on its own, but next to `structuredContent` it is dropped: `MCPTool._run` returns the structured value alone. The model gets the block as the JSON of the `TextContent` object, wrapper keys included, not its bare text.
notes.google_adk_java: Google ADK (Java) 1.11.0: `AbstractMcpTool.wrapCallResult` returns `{"text_output": [...]}`, with each text block parsed as JSON or wrapped as `{"text": ...}`. The model's `functionResponse` and the `afterToolCallback` both see that map, so the text survives but not as plain text.
notes.langchain4j: LangChain4j 1.22.0-beta32: a text-only result reaches both boundaries unchanged. When the result also carries `structuredContent`, the executor returns the structured value's JSON in place of the text blocks, so the server's own text is lost (direct `mixed_content` and `text_and_structured`: `n`).
notes.koog: Koog 1.3.0-beta: boundary-dependent. At `direct` (`EventHandler.onToolCallCompleted`) the `CallToolResult` is intact. `AIAgent` sends the tool's result to the model as one `role: tool` message whose content is `McpTool.encodeResultToString`: the JSON of the whole `CallToolResult` (`content`, `isError`, `structuredContent`), or `Error: <text>` when `isError` is set. At `agent` the text arrives inside that JSON, for example `{"content": [{"text": "SENTINEL_TEXT_BLOCK", "type": "text"}], "isError": false}`, not as bare text.
notes.google_adk_go: Google ADK (Go) 2.5.0 (go-sdk 1.8.0): a plain text result reaches the model intact as `{"output": text}`. When the result also has `structuredContent`, `mcpTool.Run` returns `{"output": structuredContent}` alone and the text blocks are dropped.
